newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to up $5 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to up $5 a tonne.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 a tonne higher on Thursday, in line with gains in London overnight, traders said.

London cocoa futures were firmer early Thursday, buoyed in part by a report from ED&F Man. LIFFE July cocoa was up seven stg at the midday break, to 1,035 stg, and Sepember rose five stg, to 1,053 stg.

ED&F Man's comment that "due to unfavourable weather, early setting for the new crops in West Africa has been the lowest since 1983" was viewed as mildly constructive for the market, London traders said.
ED&F Man also cut its 1996/97 cocoa deficit forecast to between 125,000 and 150,000 tonnes from its previous estimate in January of between 170,000 and 230,000 tonnes.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly higher, boosted by local and speculative buying. July rose $17 a tonne, to end at $1,486, after trading between $1,494 and $1,459. Second-month September also closed $17 higher, at $1,512, while the back months gained $10 to $16.

Technically, trader said if the July contract filled a chart gap between $1,494 and $1,501, the next resistance level would be near $1,515-$1.520. On the downside, July support was pegged at $1,475-$1,470.
